title: 门那边的人 · 分级读物 (HSK 3)
source_material: Original story developed from a forum post ('Met a Man in Dream for 10 Years'): a woman has met the same man in dreams for a decade; he is chained in a parallel world behind a sea or mountain gate; a prophecy says the gate opens at a certain age; he is cursed to kill her when they meet, so he avoids her; she looks for a loophole. Part one develops the ten years before the post; part two continues past it to an ending.

bible.logline: For ten years 林雨 has met a chained man in her dreams; to reach him before the gate closes she must walk into the one meeting he is cursed to end by killing her — without knowing whether he hides from her to save her, or calls her to set himself free.
bible.the_mechanism: The curse and the key are the same thing. 300 years ago the chains were locked with a girl's blood: they open only when he SEES her again — and that day he must kill her. A wicked 阿夜 would want her to come; a good one would hide. Both readings fit every fact until chapter 24.

cast.我 / 林雨: the narrator, a woman, 18 at the first dream, 28 at the end. Grew up with 奶奶 in 海城. Stubborn, honest with herself, practical in daylight. Draws.
cast.阿夜: the chained man. No name; she names him. Never looks at her, only her reflection. Speaks little.
cast.the low voice: a second voice from behind the gate, heard only when 阿夜 is absent. Turns out to be him too.
cast.奶奶: her grandmother. Raised her. Knows the legend, keeps the bell, keeps a notebook. Dies when 林雨 is 27.
cast.小美: best friend in the city since university. Loud, warm, fast. The voice of the ordinary world.
cast.老周: old fisherman, 奶奶's friend of fifty years. Knows the fishermen's version of the legend and the tides.

relationships: 林雨 and 阿夜: ten years across the water; she wants to cross, he forbids it
奶奶 raised 林雨; 老周 has been 奶奶's friend since primary school
小美 loves 林雨 and fears for her
the girl of 300 years ago was a daughter of the 林 family — 林雨's own family; the bell has stayed in the family since
setting: the dream: grey sea, grey sky, no sun or moon, no rain; two black rocks with a stone gate between; a strip of water; the man in chains beyond it
海城: small seaside town, two main streets, the harbour, 奶奶's house near the water (her room on the second floor faces the sea)
the big city: 林雨's small flat, the university, the company office
the mountain behind 海城 with an old carved stone gate
the real gate: two black rocks far out at sea; at the lowest tide of the year a stone path appears for one hour; behind the gate a cave in total darkness
motifs: water and reflection — he only ever looks at her in the water (水里的我)
rain and hot noodles — the first thing he asked about; the last scene
the bell (小铃) — rings by itself as the day comes nearer
the red line on her left wrist, matching his chains
see vs meet — the curse says 看见, not 见面
fire — the town burned 300 years ago; his hands
the forum post — opens part one, opens part two, closes the book
events: 1. 3 a.m., a week before 28: violent dream, she writes the post
2. Ten years earlier: life in 海城 with 奶奶; 老周 warns of the black rocks
3. The first dream; sand in the bed; 奶奶 goes pale
4. Dreams return; he asks about rain; she names him 阿夜
5. He only looks at her reflection; she wades in; his threat
6. University; double life; the red line appears
7. 小美; boyfriends leave; the doctor and the pills; he knows about 小美
8. At 24, 奶奶's legend and the bell; the promise
9. At 26, the curse revealed
10. He hides; the low voice; it knows what only he knows
11. At 27, 奶奶 dies; the bell rings at the funeral
12. Violent dreams, hands at her throat; back to the post
13. Replies; 小美's call; 老周's message; train home
14. 老周's version: blood lock, key = curse
15. The mountain gate; the real rocks; the tide date
16. 奶奶's box: childhood drawing, family notebook, 看见 underlined, a letter
17. Dream of 300 years ago; the curse in her own voice
18. 小美 arrives; the quarrel; making up
19. 老周's own story of the rocks; the plan; last dream
20. Birthday: grave, promise kept, departure
21. The path in the sea; the gate; the cave
22. In the dark: two voices, one man; touch
23. 'The fire was mine'; 'let me see you'
24. The light; the knife; the throw; the tide
25. After; the last post

notes.voice: First person (我 = 林雨), past tense. Chapter 1 and chapter 25 are in the present and frame the book; chapters 2–12 are the ten years before the post; 13–24 continue after it.
notes.register: HSK 3: short sentences, plain narration. Emotion goes into dialogue and small physical details (cold hands, wet feet, the bell, the red line) — never into explaining feelings at length.
notes.throughline: 我 vs 他: every chapter has at least one moment where what I want and what he wants pull apart — or, from ch17 on, where my present self pulls against the girl of 300 years ago. Keep it as a scene, not a comment.
notes.ambiguity_rule: Never let narration state what 阿夜 is. Every clue must admit both readings (he hides to save her / he lures her to free himself). Only ch23–24 resolve it. Each chapter's own note names the clue it adds.
notes.ending: Decided: he really did burn 海城 300 years ago (the dark reading is true about the past), but ten years of her stories made him someone who will not kill her (the hero reading is true about the present). She refuses the darkness loophole and turns on the light; he sees her; the chains fall; the curse lifts his hand with the knife; she holds his hand and does not run; he throws the knife into the sea. His fire goes out for good. He lives in 海城 as an ordinary man; who he is, he chooses every day. Last line: rain.
refrains: his line: 别过来。/ 回去。 (ch3 first, ch12, ch19 as 别来, ch24 inverted when he says 你过来)
下雨是什么样子的？ (ch4 question, ch25 answer)
the post's last line: 另：我可以告诉你们更多的细节。 (ch1, ch12, ch25)
水里的我 — he only sees her in the water

style_sheet.the gate: 门 / 石头门; 海门 only in 奶奶's notebook and from 老周
style_sheet.the girl from 300 years ago: 三百年前的那个女孩儿 (never 前世)
style_sheet.the man before she names him: 那个男人 / 他; after ch4 always 阿夜
style_sheet.what the town calls him: 会用火的人 (never 巫师 / 魔法)

character_voices.阿夜: very few words, short sentences. Calls her 林雨, never 小雨. Never says 爱. Answers hard questions with silence or another question. When angry, repeats: 别来，别来。
character_voices.the low voice: slower, lower; only ever says some form of 快来 / 时间不多了 / 带上铃 / 来找我. Also calls her 林雨.
character_voices.奶奶: calls her 小雨. Practical; ends hard conversations with 吃饭吧. Never says what she believes.
character_voices.小美: fast, exclamations, laughs loudly. Calls her 小雨 when tender, 林雨 when angry.
character_voices.老周: calls her 孩子. Talks about the sea and tides in plain short sentences. Gives both sides, never his own verdict.

fixed_facts: first dream: July, ten years ago, she is 18, the summer before university
red line appears on her LEFT wrist in her second year of university (age 19)
奶奶 tells the legend at New Year when 林雨 is 24; gives her the bell then
阿夜 reveals the curse in the autumn she is 26
奶奶 dies in the spring she is 27
her 28th birthday is a Saturday: no moon, the lowest tide of the year; the path opens at midnight for one hour
in the dream world it never rains and there is no sun or moon
the girl of 300 years ago was from the 林 family; the bell was hers
老周's message signs as 海城老周; he was the old man staring at the bell at the funeral
avoid: 巫师, 魔法, 前世, 灵魂, 锁链 — see the style sheet
explaining the ambiguity in narration ("maybe he is good, maybe he is bad") more than once per chapter — show the clue instead

outline.title: 凌晨三点
outline.summary: Present. 我 wakes at 3 a.m. in her city flat from the worst dream yet; her 28th birthday is next Saturday — the age when 'the gate opens'. She writes a 帖子 online asking for help, and presses send.
scenes: The dream: grey sea, the stone gate, the man in chains standing up and shouting; fire on the water; a knife in his hand, blood on it; only '别过来！' is clear. She wakes.
The flat at 3 a.m.: air conditioner hum, salt on her lips, the red line on her left wrist hot and dark. She drinks water at the window; the city lights.
The calendar: next Saturday circled — her birthday, 28. What she was told long ago: the year she is 28, the gate opens. Dreams have gone from once a week to every night.
She finds a website where people post strange experiences (a dead grandfather seen, a cat that talks) and decides to write one.

The post in full (title《我在梦里见一个男人，见了十年》): soulmate; dreams for ten years; the age; chained in another world; gate in the sea or a mountain; he may die; the curse — he must kill her when they meet, so he won't meet her; there must be a loophole; please help; 另：我可以告诉你们更多的细节。
Hesitation over the keyboard — will people think she is mad? She presses send. The little bell on her desk gives one soft ring by itself. She thinks: it all began ten years ago, that summer.
outline.notes: Clue to both sides: the knife in his hand (threat) and '别过来' (warning).
outline.recap: At 3 a.m., a week before her 28th birthday — the age when "the gate opens" — Lin Yu wakes from her worst dream yet (the chained man standing in fire with a bloody knife, shouting "don't come!"), with salt on her lips and the red line on her left wrist burning; she writes a post online about the man she has met in dreams for ten years, his chains, the gate, and the curse that he must kill her when they meet; when she presses send, the little bell on her desk rings by itself, and she remembers the summer it all began.

outline.title: 海城的夏天
outline.summary: Ten years earlier. 我 is 18 and lives with 奶奶 in seaside 海城; exams are over, she leaves for university in September. At the harbour 老周 warns that fishermen never go near two black rocks far out at sea; 奶奶 tells her not to ask. That hot night she sleeps with the window open.
scenes: 海城 introduced: two main streets, a small station, the harbour; boats out every morning, back every evening. Her parents work far away; she grew up with 奶奶 in a house by the sea, her room upstairs facing the water.
奶奶's habits: up before the sun, cooks noodles whenever it rains, ends every hard talk with '吃饭吧'. 我 is happy and sad about leaving in September.
At the harbour, an old fisherman mending a net — 老周, 奶奶's old friend — teases her: 林家的孩子长大了. She points at two black rocks far out at sea and asks about them.
老周's answer: the water there is strange; fishermen don't go; even the fish don't. He changes the subject.
At dinner she asks 奶奶 about the rocks. 奶奶's chopsticks stop. 'Don't go there. Don't ask.' Then: '吃饭吧。'
Hot July night, window open. Lying in bed she hears the sea, and under it, for a second, something like metal dragging on stone. She falls asleep.
outline.notes: Seed 老周, the rocks, and 奶奶's fear. No dream yet — end on the edge of it.
outline.recap: Ten years earlier, 18-year-old Lin Yu lives with her grandmother in the small seaside town of Haicheng, about to leave for university in September; at the harbour old Zhou, Grandma's friend, tells her fishermen never go near the two black rocks far out at sea and changes the subject; at dinner Grandma says "don't go there, don't ask — let's eat"; that hot night, falling asleep with the window open, Lin Yu thinks she hears something like a chain dragging on stone beneath the sound of the sea — and dreams of him for the first time.

outline.title: 第一个梦
outline.summary: The first dream: grey sea, two black rocks, a stone gate, a young man in chains beyond a strip of water who will not look at her and says 'go back, don't come'. She wakes with wet sand on her feet; at breakfast 奶奶 goes pale.
scenes: The dream world: not 海城's blue sea but grey; grey sky, no sun, no moon; strong wind with no sound. The two black rocks like two standing people; between them an old stone gate covered in carvings she can't read.

Beyond the gate, a strip of water; beyond the water, a young man in black, long hair, chains on hands and feet running into the water. Her heart hurts at the sight of him, as if she has known him a long time.
She calls to him. He does not turn his face; he looks only at the water. Low, tired voice: '回去。别过来。' 'Why?' '回去。以后也别再来了。'
She steps forward; icy water at her feet. She wakes. Morning, boats already out. Her feet are wet; there is wet cold sand in the bed. Window on the second floor, door closed.
Breakfast: she asks 奶奶 if there is a stone gate in the sea. 奶奶's hand stops while serving porridge; she goes white: 'who told you?' 'A dream.' Long look. '吃饭吧，饭要凉了。'
That evening 我 sees 奶奶 sitting alone at the door, looking at the sea a long time. Two quiet nights follow; 我 almost decides it was nothing.
outline.notes: Clue: he refuses to look at her — tenderness or danger, the reader can't tell yet.
outline.recap: In the first dream Lin Yu stands by a grey, silent sea with no sun or moon, before a carved stone gate between two black rocks; beyond a strip of water sits a young man in black with long hair and chains on his hands and feet, who will not look at her and tells her "go back, don't come, and never come again"; she steps forward into icy water and wakes with wet feet and cold sand in her bed; when she asks Grandma about a stone gate in the sea, Grandma turns white, trembles, says only "let's eat", and that night sits alone in the dark at the door staring at the sea; two dreamless nights follow and Lin Yu almost believes it was nothing.

outline.title: 下雨是什么样子的
outline.summary: The dreams return, every few days. He won't speak, so she talks. One night he asks what rain is like. She names him 阿夜. A ritual grows: each night she brings him one thing from her world.
scenes: A week later, the grey sea again; then again; soon every three or four days. Always him on the far side, her on the near side, the water and the gate between.
At first he says nothing and won't answer; she feels he is waiting for her to give up. She doesn't: she talks — her name, 海城, 奶奶's fish, her fear of the big city.

Mid-sentence one night he speaks: '下雨，是什么样子的？' He has no rain, no wind, no day there — only water. She describes rain: soft spring rain like someone speaking softly to your face; long summer rain; 奶奶's hot noodles while listening to it.
He starts asking: what noodles taste like, how fast trains are, what people do at school. He listens like it's the best story in the world. He never talks about himself.
Names: 'I have none. I used to, not now.' She names him 阿夜 because he only comes at night. He doesn't answer, but from then on when she says 阿夜 he lifts his head.
She begins to save things from each day to tell him. One night, when she leaves, he says '谢谢' — the first time. In September she leaves 海城 for the city, wondering if he will follow.
outline.notes: Clue: his hunger for her world — a lonely good man learning, or a prisoner studying the outside. Plant 'soft rain like someone speaking softly to your face' word for word: ch25 echoes it.
outline.recap: The dreams return every few days; the man never speaks, so Lin Yu talks — about Haicheng, the boats, Grandma's fish — until one night he suddenly asks what rain is like, since where he is there is no rain, wind, day or night, only water; she describes spring rain "like someone speaking softly to your face" and Grandma's hot noodles on rainy days; he begins asking about noodles, trains, school, but says he has no name, so she names him A Ye ("Night"); she starts saving small things from each day to tell him, he thanks her for the first time, and in September she leaves for the city wondering if he will follow.

outline.title: 水里的我
outline.summary: She realises he never looks at her face, only her reflection in the water. She tries to make him look; when she wades in toward him, he stands, chains roaring, and threatens never to come back. First open clash.
scenes: On the first night in the city he is there: 'you went far — the water sounds different.' Relief.
She notices: he looks at the water, at 水里的我, never at her. She tests it: moves along the bank so her reflection leaves the water — he closes his eyes until it returns.
She asks him to tell her what she looks like. He describes her reflection exactly, down to a small mark by her eyebrow. 'You see me perfectly — so look at me!' 'This is enough.' 'Not for me.'
She walks into the water: ankles, knees, thighs, freezing. He stands up; every chain sounds at once like thunder. '停下！再走一步，我就再也不来了。再也不。' First time he raises his voice.
She stops in the water. His head is down, chains still moving. 'Why won't you let me come?' Long silence. '回去吧，林雨。天快亮了。'
She wakes with both legs and her trousers wet. She thinks: what I want and what he wants are not the same. She doesn't know they will argue about it for ten years.
outline.notes: The throughline made explicit once. Clue: the threat to vanish — protection or control.
outline.recap: On her first night in the city Lin Yu fears the dream won't come, but A Ye is there and knows she has gone far "because the water sounds different"; she realises he never looks at her face, only her reflection — when she moves out of the water's view he shuts his eyes — though he describes her perfectly, down to a tiny mole above her eyebrow; when she wades in to make him look at her he stands, chains roaring, and says if she takes one more step he will never come back; she stops, gets no answer but "go back, Lin Yu, it's almost light", and wakes soaked to the waist, knowing for the first time that what she wants and what he wants are not the same.

outline.title: 两个世界
outline.summary: University and then work in the city: by day an ordinary student, by night beside the grey sea. In her second year a red line appears on her left wrist exactly where his chains are, darker after bad dreams.
scenes: The city: tall buildings, wide roads, lights brighter than stars, cars instead of waves. Her days: classes, exams, canteen, library.
Her nights: she tells him about the city — the underground, crowds, a hundred kinds of noodles. He asks why people in a city of millions walk without looking at each other.
Second year: a thin red line around her left wrist, like a red watch. She thinks she scratched it; it doesn't fade.
She notices in the dream: the line is exactly where his chain sits. After bad dreams it turns darker, once red as blood. She starts wearing long sleeves even in summer.
She asks him about it. He looks at the water a long time: 'does it hurt?' 'A little.' '...I'm sorry.' He won't say more.
Graduation; a job at a company; a small flat of her own. Years pass with two lives that never touch — except at her wrist.
outline.notes: Clue: the red line — a bond they share, or a brand that marks her as his.
outline.recap: In the city Lin Yu lives two lives — an ordinary student by day, beside the grey sea by night — telling A Ye about the underground, a hundred kinds of noodles, and crowds who never look at each other, which moves him ("I'm alone here and want to see one person every day; you're all together and look at no one"); in her second year a red line appears around her left wrist, exactly where his chain sits, darker after bad dreams, so she wears long sleeves even in summer; shown it, he only asks "does it hurt?" and says "I'm sorry", refusing to explain; she graduates, works as a designer, rents a small flat — two worlds that never touch except at her wrist.

outline.title: 小美
outline.summary: 小美 becomes her best friend. Two boyfriends leave her ('there's always someone between us'). 小美 finds notebooks full of one man's face and sends her to a doctor; the pills stop the dreams and she feels empty, so she throws them away. That night he asks: 'who is 小美?'
scenes: 小美: university classmate, clever, warm, talks fast, laughs loudest in any room; the person she trusts most in the city.
Two boyfriends: the classmate ('your heart is always somewhere else') and the colleague ('it's like there's a third person with us'). Both are right.
小美 visits and finds the notebook: page after page of the same man's face. 'New boyfriend?' 我 tells half the truth — the dreams, many years — and shows the wrist.
小美, serious: '小雨, you're tired, you're under pressure — see a doctor. Dreams are only dreams.' 我 isn't angry; she has thought it herself.
The doctor: stress, sleep problems, pills. A week without dreams. She sleeps well — and feels as if someone has died. On the eighth night she throws the pills away.
The dream returns. Before she speaks, he says: '你一个星期没来。' Then: '小美是谁？' She never told him about 小美. Which frightens her more: that he lives only in her head, or that he doesn't?
outline.notes: Me vs the other at its most ordinary: her life against him. Clue: he knows things he shouldn't — closeness, or surveillance.
outline.recap: Lin Yu's best friend Xiaomei — loud, warm, fast-talking — has been at her side since university; two boyfriends leave her, both feeling "someone else is between us"; Xiaomei finds a notebook full of drawings of the same man, hears half the truth, sees the red line, and gently urges a doctor; the doctor prescribes sleeping pills and for a week Lin Yu sleeps without dreams — and feels as if someone has died; she throws the pills away, and that night A Ye says flatly "you didn't come for a week" and then asks "who is Xiaomei?" — a name she has never told him.

outline.title: 奶奶的故事
outline.summary: At 24, home for New Year, she asks 奶奶 about the gate again. 奶奶 tells the town legend of the man who came out of the sea and held fire, the night 海城 burned, and the girl who chained him and never came back — 'the year she is 28, the gate opens' — and gives 我 the girl's little bell.
scenes: New Year's Eve in 海城: 奶奶 older, hair all white; dumplings; fireworks over the sea turning it red and green; the kitchen, hot tea.
我 asks again about the stone gate; she has been dreaming six years. 奶奶's hands tremble: 'I hoped the city would make you forget.'
The legend: 300 years ago a man walked out of the sea, dry; he could hold fire in his hands without pain; the town feared him; one girl did not — she brought him food, they fell in love.

Then one night the town burned all night; people died; someone saw him standing in the fire. Next day the town and the girl took chains, rowed him between the black rocks and chained him beyond the gate. The girl never came back.

'Was he bad?' Some old people say he set the fire to burn the whole town; others that he stood in it to put it out and save people. Nobody alive saw it. And the old saying: she will come back — the year she is 28, the gate opens.

奶奶 brings a small wooden box: an old black bell, handed down from her own grandmother — 'it was that girl's'. When it touches 我's hand, the red line stings. 奶奶 makes her promise: if she ever goes to find the gate, she comes home and tells 奶奶 first. 我 promises — and later breaks it.
outline.notes: Both readings stated aloud by the town. Plant that the bell has always stayed in their family.
outline.recap: At 24 Lin Yu comes home to Haicheng for New Year and finds Grandma much older; on New Year's Eve, after six years of dreams, she asks about the stone gate again and Grandma finally tells the town legend — 300 years ago a dry man walked out of the sea who could hold fire, shunned by all but one girl who fed him and fell in love with him; one night the town burned, he was seen standing in the fire, and the townspeople and the girl chained him beyond the gate between the black rocks; the girl never returned; some say he set the fire, others that he was fighting it; "the year she is 28, the gate opens"; Grandma gives Lin Yu the girl's ancient bell, kept in their family for generations — it makes the red line sting — and makes her promise to come home and tell her first if she ever goes looking for the gate.

outline.title: 他的秘密
outline.summary: At 26 she finally asks 阿夜 whether he is the man of the legend. He won't answer, but tells her the curse: the day he sees her, his hands will kill her. That is why he only looks at the water. 'If you love me, don't look for me.'
scenes: Two years she keeps the story to herself — afraid of a yes and of a no. An autumn night she sits down in the dream and finds the bell in her hand; it came with her.
He stares at the bell in the water: 'where did you get that?' 'My 奶奶.' She tells him the legend and asks: '那个人，是你吗？' Total silence; she can hear her own heartbeat.
He doesn't answer. Instead: 'I'll tell you one thing; after it you must not come again.' The curse: 我看见你的那一天，就必须杀了你. 'Not me — my hands. That day they won't obey me. I'll pick up a knife...'
She understands: ten years of 水里的我. 'Who cursed you?' No answer. 'Is that the only reason you won't let me come?' 'It is the only reason.'
'林雨，要是你爱我，就不要来找我。' She wakes with her face wet with tears.
In the city that week she walks around in a daze; 小美 notices; 我 says she slept badly. She looks at her wrist and thinks: he is protecting me — or he wants me to believe he is.
outline.notes: Clue: he refuses to say whether he is the legend's man — modesty about guilt, or concealment.
outline.recap: For two years Lin Yu keeps Grandma's story to herself, afraid of either answer; one autumn night at 26 the bell appears in her hand inside the dream, and when she tells A Ye the legend and asks "is that man you?" he won't answer, but reveals the curse — the day he sees her, his hands will make him pick up a knife and kill her — which is the "only reason" he has looked only at her reflection and kept her away; he still won't say whether he is the man from the legend, only "if you love me, don't come looking for me"; she wakes in tears, drifts through a dazed week that Xiaomei notices, and for the first time wonders whether he is protecting her or wants her to believe he is.

outline.title: 另一个声音
outline.summary: 阿夜 starts hiding: empty chains, only his voice saying 'go back'. On nights he is absent a lower, slower voice behind the gate says 'come quickly, time is short, bring the bell'. She tests it — it knows what only 阿夜 knows.
scenes: Night after night the far bank is empty: chains lying on the stone, nobody in them. His voice from far away: '回去吧。别找我。' She walks the grey shore till dawn. The more he hides, the more she wants to find him.
A winter night: from behind the gate, from somewhere very dark, a voice — like 阿夜's but lower, slower: '快来。时间不多了。' 'A Ye? Is it you?' '来找我，林雨。带上那个铃。' Then nothing.
It comes again on other empty nights, always saying the same few things. She decides to test it: 'What was the first thing you ever asked me?' Pause. '下雨。' Only 阿夜 could know that.
When 阿夜 finally appears again she tells him. He goes very still: '门后面什么也没有。别听它。' 'It knew about the rain.' He doesn't answer.
One A Ye says: don't come, you'll die. The other: come, time is short. Maybe both are him; maybe neither. Her question is no longer whether to trust him but which him.
She starts writing down every dream in a notebook in the city: dates, words, the colour of the red line.
outline.notes: Core ambiguity device. Clue: the voice knows his secrets — it is him (so he lures her), or something that has listened to him for 300 years.
outline.recap: A Ye begins hiding: night after night only empty chains lie on the stone and his distant voice says "go back, don't look for me"; then, on a winter night when he is absent, a lower, slower voice from behind the gate says "come quickly, time is short — come find me, Lin Yu, bring the bell"; it keeps returning when he is gone, so she tests it by asking the first question A Ye ever asked her, and it answers "rain" — something only he could know; when A Ye returns, thinner, he says "there is nothing behind the gate, don't listen to it," but won't say whether the voice is his; she no longer knows which A Ye to believe, and starts keeping a written record of every dream.

outline.title: 奶奶走了
outline.summary: In the spring she is 27, 奶奶 dies in her sleep before 我 can keep her promise. At the funeral the bell in 我's bag rings by itself; an old man stares at it, pale, and says nothing. Her first night alone in 奶奶's house.
scenes: A meeting at work; her phone; the neighbour 阿姨 from 海城: 奶奶 didn't get up this morning; she went quietly, as if asleep.
The night train. 奶奶's house unchanged: her teacup on the kitchen table, half full. 我 stands at the door unable to go in. The promise she can no longer keep.
The funeral: grey sky, strong wind off the sea, many old people, nobody speaking.

In her bag something rings: 叮——叮——. The bell, moving and ringing on its own though nothing touches it. Everyone looks. One old man with a weathered face goes white and stares at it, says nothing. (老周 — not named yet.)
The neighbour gives her 奶奶's last words to pass on: '告诉小雨，她答应我的事，别忘了。'
That night alone in 奶奶's house, the bell by the bed; at midnight it rings once more. She doesn't dream of 阿夜 at all — only of 奶奶 cooking noodles while it rains.
outline.notes: Grief, and the promise. Clue: the bell wakes as he weakens — a warning, or a summons.
outline.recap: In the spring she is 27, Lin Yu gets a call at work from Grandma's neighbour Aunt Wang: Grandma died quietly in her sleep; Lin Yu takes the night train home to an unchanged house with Grandma's half-drunk tea on the table, unable to keep her promise now; at the funeral the bell in her bag rings by itself, and a tall, weathered old man at the back stares at it, white-faced, then disappears; Aunt Wang passes on Grandma's last words — "tell Xiaoyu not to forget what she promised me"; alone in her childhood room the bell rings again at midnight, and instead of A Ye she dreams of Grandma making noodles in the rain and saying "let's eat".

outline.title: 时间不多了
outline.summary: After the funeral the dreams turn violent: old wooden 海城 burning, 阿夜 bloody in the fire, chains breaking; one night his cold hands close on her throat while he says 'go, go quickly' — she wakes with finger marks. He grows thin and weak. Half a year later it is three a.m. and she writes the post.
scenes: Before, the dreams were strange but quiet. Now: an old 海城 of wooden houses burning, red sky, people running and screaming.
阿夜 standing in the fire, blood on his face and hands — his or someone else's, she can't tell.
The chains across the water breaking one by one, until only the one on his left wrist is left, red as fire.
The worst dream: he finally crosses the water, head down, never looking at her face, and puts both hands on her throat. Cold as sea water. She can't scream or run. In her ear, urgently: '走！快走！'
She wakes before dawn; in the bathroom mirror, two red rows of finger marks on her neck. Was he killing her — or pushing her away from something? From his own hands?

He grows thinner, more tired; she feels he is dying. Half a year passes with a clock ticking inside her. Then it is the week before her birthday, three a.m., salt on her lips — she writes the post. Now you know. These are the details.
outline.notes: Ambiguity at its peak. Close by echoing ch1's post and its last line.
outline.recap: After Grandma's death the dreams turn violent — old wooden Haicheng burning under a red sky, A Ye standing still in the fire with blood on his face and hands, his chains breaking one dream at a time until only the one on his left wrist remains, red as fire; one night he crosses the water, head down, puts his ice-cold hands around her throat and tightens them while urging "go! Lin Yu, go quickly!" — she wakes with finger marks on her neck, unsure whether he was killing her or pushing her away from his own hands; he grows paler and weaker, and half a year later, the week before her birthday, she wakes at 3 a.m. and writes the post — "these are the details."

outline.title: 网上的回答
outline.summary: The morning after the post: mockery, advice, one believer. 小美 calls in alarm. At noon a private message from '海城老周': he knows the gate, 奶奶 told him about her, come home. She takes a week off and the train home with six days left; on the train 阿夜 appears, angry for the first time.
scenes: 7 a.m.: dozens of replies. 'Write a novel!' 'He wants to kill you and you want to find him? Are you stupid?' 'Fake.' 'See a doctor, seriously.' One: 'I believe you. I dreamed of someone for three years; then I saw him at a station. He didn't know me.'
8 a.m.: 小美 calls: she recognised it at once. 'In the dream or not, he wants to kill you!' She makes 我 promise to wait for her that evening.

Noon: a private message signed 海城老周 — 'I know that gate. Your 奶奶 told me about you. She said if you came looking, I should help. I'm at the 海城 harbour. Come home. Time is short.' 我 never wrote her name or her town.
She remembers the pale old man at the funeral. She packs fast, before she can think: clothes, the bell. Calls her manager: a week's leave, family matters. Calendar: six days.
She texts 小美 ('I've gone back to 海城. Don't worry.'), switches her phone off, takes the underground to the station.

On the train she falls asleep: 阿夜, back turned, chains dragging, angry for the first time: 'Why are you going back? Get off at the next station.' 'Because you tell me nothing!' '...You'll regret it.' 'That's my business.' The announcement: 海城站到了。Grey-blue sea outside.
outline.notes: Clue: he knows where she is going — and is furious; fear for her, or fear of being found out.
outline.recap: The morning after the post, over a hundred replies — jokes, insults, "see a doctor", and one person who dreamed of a man for three years, then met him at a station and he asked "who are you?"; Xiaomei calls in alarm and makes Lin Yu promise to wait for her; at noon a private message from "Haicheng Old Zhou" says he knows the gate, Grandma told him about her, come home, time is short — though she never wrote her name or town; she recognises him as the old man at the funeral and the net-mender of ten years ago, takes a week's leave, packs the bell and her dream notebook and catches the train with six days left; asleep on the train she finds A Ye for the first time in many nights, his back to her, angry for the first time, ordering her off at the next station and warning she'll regret it — and she wakes in Haicheng.

outline.title: 老周
outline.summary: At the harbour she meets 老周, the old man from the funeral, 奶奶's friend of fifty years, who searched the internet for half a year to find her. Over tea he tells the fishermen's version: the girl locked the chains with her own blood and life; they open only when he sees her again — and that day he must kill her. The key and the curse are one.
scenes: The harbour unchanged: boats, fish, salt air. An old man mending a net beside a small boat looks up, not surprised: '你来了。我是老周。坐吧。' She recognises him from the funeral — and from the summer she was 18.
His small clean house by the harbour; tea. He and 奶奶 were primary-school classmates, friends for fifty years. Before she died 奶奶 told him everything about 小雨's dreams.
How he found her: his grandson taught him to use the internet; for half a year he searched every day for 石头门, 链子, 二十八岁.

'Your 奶奶 told you the town's story. We fishermen have another — my grandfather to my father to me.' No chain could hold a man who held fire. So the girl cut her hand and put her blood on the lock: she locked him with her own life.
Since then one thing opens the lock: he sees her again. That day the chains break — and that day he must kill her. 'The key and the curse are the same thing, child.'

'If he is bad, he'll wait for you and find ways to make you come. If he is good, he'll hide, push you away, scold you. But a clever bad man would also tell you not to come — he knows the more he forbids it, the more you'll go. From here, child, they look the same.' 'Then how can I know?' '只有一个办法：见到他。' That night she waits for 阿夜; only the low voice comes, very far away, saying her name.
outline.notes: The mechanism stated plainly. 老周 gives both sides, no verdict.
outline.recap: At the harbour Lin Yu finds old Zhou mending nets exactly as ten years before; in his small house a photo shows him and Grandma at sixteen — friends for over sixty years; Grandma told him Lin Yu would come, "stubborn like her"; he found the post after searching online for half a year, and when the bell rang at the funeral he knew the time had come; he tells the fishermen's version: no chain could hold the fire-man, so the girl cut her hand and locked him with her own blood and life — the lock opens only when he sees her again, and that same day he must kill her: "the key and the curse are the same thing"; a bad man would lure her, a good one would push her away — but a clever bad man would also forbid her; "from here they look the same; the only way is to meet him"; that night A Ye doesn't come, only the low voice calling her name.

outline.title: 山上的门
outline.summary: 老周 takes her up the mountain behind 海城 to the old stone gate many think is the one from the legend. It is only a picture: carvings of a man walking out of the sea with fire, the man and a woman, the town burning, the chained man facing a woman with a knife. The bell does nothing. From the far side she sees the two black rocks; the path to them opens only at the year's lowest tide — next Saturday night, moonless, her birthday.
scenes: The climb: a mountain not high but hard; 奶奶 never let her go as a child. 老周 talks while walking: 'many say this is the gate; I don't think so. You'll see.' The path narrows, trees thicken; two hours.
The stone gate: two stones and one across the top, like her dream gate but smaller; nothing inside but mountain and wind. She walks through and back. Nothing.

The carvings, one by one: a man from the sea with fire in his hand; the man and a woman together; many fires, many houses; the man in chains, the woman before him holding a knife — to kill him, to cut her own hand, or to give it to him? Last: only sea and two black rocks.
She rings the bell inside the gate: 叮—— Nothing. '这个门，只是一张画。真的门不在这里。'

老周 leads her round to the other side of the summit: all of 海城, and far out the two black rocks, one left, one right, like two standing people. Her heart stops: 'that's it — that's where I go in my dreams.'

The tide: the water there is strange; only on the lowest tide of the year does a path appear between them; at other times no boat gets through. 'Which day?' He hesitates. 'Next Saturday night. The night with no moon.' Her birthday.
outline.notes: Clue: the carving of the woman with the knife — who holds the blade, and for whom.
outline.recap: Old Zhou leads Lin Yu up the mountain behind Haicheng, revealing that Grandma climbed it once at seventeen and afterwards said "our family must never come here again"; the old stone gate at the top resembles her dream gate but is smaller and opens onto nothing, and its carvings show a man walking out of the sea with fire, a woman bringing him food, the town burning, and the chained man facing the woman holding a knife — whether to kill him, cut her hand, or give it to him is unclear; the bell rings without effect: "this gate is only a picture"; from the far side she sees the two black rocks of her dream, reachable only when a path appears at the lowest tide of the year — next Saturday night, the moonless night of her birthday; on the way down Zhou suggests the carving was meant to warn that the knife is still there.

outline.title: 奶奶的箱子
outline.summary: Alone in 奶奶's house she finds an old box under the bed: photos, a drawing she made at six of a man in chains (twelve years before the first dream), and 奶奶's notebook — the girl was a daughter of the 林 family; the curse copied out with 看见 underlined and 'see, not meet' beside it; and a letter to 小雨. The loophole: meet him where he cannot see her.
scenes: Back from the mountain, the empty house; she looks for anything 奶奶 left. Under 奶奶's bed, an old wooden box.

Photos: young 奶奶 with 老周 and other children at the harbour; 我 as a baby. Her old homework. And a child's drawing in crayon: a grey sea, two black rocks, a man with lines on his hands and feet. In 奶奶's hand on the back: 小雨，六岁. Twelve years before the first dream.
The notebook: 海城's old stories. A page of family names going back many generations; beside one, 300 years ago, a girl's name and 奶奶's note: 铃是她的。她是林家的女儿。 The girl was family.
On a later page 奶奶 copied the curse as old people said it: 门那边的人，看见她的那天，锁会开，链会断。看见她的那天，他必须杀她。 Two lines under 看见; in small hurried writing: 是'看见'，不是'见面'。
Folded in the back, a letter: '小雨，要是你在看这封信，你已经回来了，可是奶奶不在了。……我一直怕。我怕你去，也怕你不去。不要因为怕去，也不要因为怕不去。……吃饭吧，别饿着。' She cries a long time.
Then she thinks: if he can't see me — a moonless night, a dark place. She has found the little door in the curse. And she thinks of the drawing: has he been with me since I was six?
outline.notes: Clue: the childhood drawing — he has watched over her all her life, or reached for her long before she could choose.
outline.recap: Alone in Grandma's house Lin Yu finally opens her things and finds an old wooden box under the bed: photos (young Grandma with Zhou at the harbour), Lin Yu's childhood drawings — including one of a grey sea, two black rocks, a gate and a chained figure, labelled by Grandma "Xiaoyu, age six", twelve years before her first dream; Grandma's notebook traces the Lin family back 300 years to a girl beside whose name is written "the bell was hers; she was a daughter of the Lin family", copies the curse with 看见 ("see") underlined and the note "see, not meet", and holds a letter: Grandma has been afraid since that drawing, afraid of her going and of her not going; "don't do a thing because you're afraid, don't not do it because you're afraid"; "you are Lin Yu, not the girl of 300 years ago"; after crying in the dark, Lin Yu sees the loophole — a moonless night, a dark place: meet him where he cannot see her.

outline.title: 三百年前
outline.summary: A different dream: she is the girl of 300 years ago in burning wooden 海城. She finds a younger 阿夜 at the harbour with fire pouring from his hands — she cannot tell if it is leaving his hands or being drawn back into them. The town comes with chains; he says 'quickly, lock me'; she cuts her hand onto the lock, and the curse comes out of her own mouth. She wakes with a faint old scar on her palm.
scenes: No grey sea, no gate: she is a barefoot girl in old clothes on a street of wooden houses — 海城, 300 years ago. Red sky; everything burning: houses, trees, boats.
People running and crying; a mother with a child; an old man sitting before his burning house saying nothing. Hot black air; she can barely breathe. She is looking for someone.

At the harbour, in the middle of the fire: 阿夜 — younger, shorter hair, no chains, not yet tired. Fire pours from his hands, bright as the sun. The terrible thing: she can't tell whether the fire is going out of his hands or coming back into them.
He sees her — the first time his eyes look straight at her, not at water: '别过来！' The townspeople arrive with chains, knives, wood: '就是他！杀了那个会用火的人！' He doesn't run. He looks at them, then at her.

Fragments, as if seen through deep water: heavy cold chains on his hands and feet; 'quickly, lock me' — to them or to her?; a knife put in her hand; she cuts her palm; her blood on the lock. A clear cold voice, every word a stone: '你再看见我的那一天，锁会开。你再看见我的那一天，你必须杀了我。' It is her own voice.

His eyes — anger? grief? thanks? — then he lowers his head and never looks at her again. She wakes crying; on her left palm a faint old line like a scar. What if the curse wasn't put on him by others? What if the one he has been fighting for ten years is her — the girl of 300 years ago?
outline.notes: Me vs the other turns inward. Clue: 'lock me' — a good man asking to be stopped, or a bad man with no choice.
outline.recap: Lin Yu dreams she is the barefoot girl of 300 years ago in burning wooden Haicheng, searching for him before the town does; at the harbour she finds a younger, unchained A Ye with fire pouring from his hands — she cannot tell whether it is leaving his hands or being drawn back into them; he looks straight at her for the first time and shouts "don't come!"; the townspeople arrive with chains and knives crying "kill the man who uses fire"; he doesn't run and lets them chain him, saying "quickly, lock me" — to them or to her; an old man puts a knife in her hand, she cuts her palm and her blood runs onto the lock, and the curse — "the day you see me again, the lock will open; that day you must kill me" — comes out of her own mouth; he lowers his head and never looks at her again; she wakes with a faint old scar on her palm, wondering if she cursed him and has been fighting her own past self all along.

outline.title: 小美来了
outline.summary: 小美 arrives in 海城, furious and frightened. On the beach 我 tells her everything; they quarrel — 'you are throwing away your life for a man in a dream' / 'he is more real than my life' — and both cry. 小美 decides to stay and wait on the beach that night.
scenes: Friday afternoon: 我 helping 老周 mend nets; someone shouting her name — 小美 dragging a big suitcase, hair a mess, a night on the train behind her. '林雨！Why has your phone been off? I called you a hundred times!' Then she hugs her hard: 'You scared me to death.'

Evening on the beach, dark blue sea, wind. 我 tells her everything: 奶奶's story, 老周's story, the mountain gate, the notebook and the letter, the dream of 300 years ago. Nothing held back. 小美 listens without a word.

小美: 'So tomorrow night you'll walk out into the sea alone to find a man from a dream who might be a bad man and might kill you.' 'If he can't see me he won't —' 'How do you know the curse is real? The gate? How do you know HE is real?'

小美 shouting now: 'You have a job, friends, me. For ten years you've lived in a dream! You're giving up your own life for a man in a dream!' 我: 'He's not a man in a dream! He's more real than my life!' Silence; waves coming and going at their feet.

小美 is crying — 我 has never seen her cry. 'I'm just afraid that after tomorrow I'll never see you again.' 我, crying too: 'If I don't go, I'll spend my whole life asking whether I was mad. I don't want that.'
小美 wipes her eyes: 'Fine. But I'm coming. Not on the boat — I'll wait on the beach. I'll wait until you come back. If you don't, I'll walk into the sea myself to get you.' 我 laughs while crying.
outline.notes: Me vs the other at the human level: the ordinary world claims her one last time. No 阿夜 in this chapter except as the subject of the fight.
outline.recap: On Friday Xiaomei turns up at the harbour, dishevelled after a night on the train, furious that Lin Yu's phone was off for days — then hugs her: "you scared me to death"; walking on the beach at dusk Lin Yu tells her everything from the first dream to the dream of 300 years ago; Xiaomei sums it up — walking into the sea to find a dream man who may have burned a town and is cursed to kill her — asks how she knows any of it is real, and shouts that she has given up ten years of her life for a dream; Lin Yu shouts back that he is more real than her life; Xiaomei, who never cries, sobs that she's afraid of never reaching her again; Lin Yu says if she doesn't go she'll wonder all her life whether she was mad; Xiaomei decides to wait on the beach — "if you don't come back, I'll walk into the sea myself, though I can't swim."

outline.title: 老周的故事
outline.summary: That night 老周 explains the plan: midnight tomorrow, the lowest tide, a path for exactly one hour. He tells his own story: at seventeen, lost in fog, he drifted near the rocks and a voice said 'go back' — he obeyed, and has wondered all his life what would have happened. Her last dream: no 阿夜, no chain, only his voice: 'don't come.'
scenes: At 老周's table with 小美: the calendar. Tomorrow: the lowest tide of the year and no moon. At midnight the path between the rocks appears. It lasts one hour. After that the sea comes back — whether she has found him or not.

Practical things: warm clothes, shoes that don't slip, the bell. 'Your phone — keep it switched off. Any light at all, and he can see you.' 小美 will hold a big lamp on the beach so 我 can find the way back.
小美 asks 老周 whether he believes any of it. He is quiet, then tells a story he has told no one but 奶奶.

At seventeen he took his father's boat out alone; fog came down; he lost the way and drifted toward the black rocks. In the fog, close by, a man's voice: '回去。' Just that. He turned the boat and rowed until his hands bled.
'Was it him?' 'I don't know. He saved my life — or he didn't want anyone near his door. I've thought about it for sixty years.' (The same word 阿夜 says to her.)

That night 我's last dream before the night: grey sea, the gate — and on the far side nothing, not even the chains. Only the black door. A long wait. Then his voice, the one she knows: '别来。' Nothing more, and the low voice doesn't come either. She wakes: it is Saturday. She is 28.
outline.notes: Clue: '回去' to the young 老周 — saving a stranger, or guarding the door. Same words as ch3.
outline.recap: Over dinner at old Zhou's, he explains the plan: tomorrow at midnight, the lowest tide and the moonless night, a path opens between the rocks for exactly one hour, and the sea waits for no one; they prepare warm clothes, non-slip shoes, the bell, and the phone kept switched off since any light would let him see her, while Xiaomei will hold a big lamp on the beach to guide her back; asked if he believes, Zhou tells a story he has only told Grandma — at seventeen, lost in sudden fog, his boat drifted toward the black rocks until a tired man's voice nearby said "go back", and he rowed till his hands bled; for sixty years he has wondered whether the voice saved him or guarded its door — the same words A Ye said to her; in her last dream there is no A Ye and no chain, only his voice saying "don't come", and she wakes on Saturday, 28 years old.

outline.title: 生日
outline.summary: Her birthday. 小美's small cake; 老周's birthday noodles, as 奶奶 used to make. She goes to 奶奶's grave and, at last, keeps her promise: 'I'm going to the gate. I came to tell you first.' At eleven at night they set out: 小美 on the beach with the lamp, 老周's boat toward the rocks.
scenes: Morning: nobody says happy birthday. 小美 has bought a small cake; the three of them sit looking at it, nobody eating.
老周 cooks a bowl of noodles: 'On your birthday you eat noodles. Your 奶奶 made them for you every year, didn't she?' Eating, 我 thinks of 奶奶; the noodles taste almost the same.
Afternoon: 奶奶's grave on the hill above the sea. 我 brings the bell. '奶奶，我要去找那个门了。我先来告诉你。' The promise kept a year late. Wind; the bell rings once in her hand.
She sits a long time telling 奶奶 everything — 阿夜, the curse, the letter. 'You said: don't go because you're afraid, don't stay because you're afraid. I'm afraid. But I'm not going because I'm afraid.'
Evening at 老周's: checking things — clothes, shoes, the bell, the phone switched off. 小美 tries to joke and fails.

11 p.m.: no moon, almost no stars; sea and sky both black. 小美 on the beach with the big lamp: 'I'm not going anywhere. When you come back, look for this light.' A hug without words. 老周's old steady boat moves out, its small lamp lighting only a little water ahead.
outline.notes: The promise motif closes. Quiet chapter before the climax — keep it tender, no dream.
outline.recap: On her birthday Xiaomei buys a small cake no one eats, and old Zhou cooks birthday noodles with an egg as Grandma used to; Lin Yu climbs to Grandma's grave above the sea with white flowers and the bell and finally keeps her promise — "I'm going to find the gate tonight; I came to tell you first" — and the bell rings once; she tells Grandma everything and says she is going not out of fear but to learn who he is and who she is; that evening she checks her things, phone switched off, while Xiaomei fails at jokes and calls her the least ordinary person she knows; at 11 p.m., under no moon, Xiaomei stays on the beach with the big lamp and old Zhou's boat carries Lin Yu toward the black rocks, the lamp behind her like a single star.

outline.title: 海里的路
outline.summary: Near midnight the sea draws back and a stone path appears. 我 walks it alone, bell in hand, phone off, to the two black rocks; she touches the real gate for the first time; the bell rings once; she steps through — not into the grey dream sea but into a cave of total darkness. Chains drag on stone. A voice: 'you came.'
scenes: 老周 stops the boat where the water gets too shallow. They wait; only the wind. Then the sea starts moving backwards — slowly, then faster, as if someone on the far side were pulling it away.
Stones rise out of the black water: one, two, ten — a path from the boat to between the rocks. '去吧。一个小时。记住，一个小时。' She climbs down.

The walk: wet slippery stones, seaweed, black water on both sides that she hears but can't see. Ten minutes or ten years. She thinks of the first dream, of rain and noodles, of his hands on her throat. Which one is he? She is about to know.
The rocks, bigger than in the dream, like two tall people standing in the night. Between them the gate. She touches it: cold, wet, real. A thousand times in dreams; the first time with her hand.

The bell rings by itself: 叮—— She takes a deep breath and walks through. On the other side: not the grey sea — a cave. Dark as nothing she has known; she can't see her own hand before her eyes. She dares not move.
Deep in the cave, chains dragging slowly over stone. A voice in the dark: '你来了。' — the low voice, the one that told her to come. Then, in 阿夜's words: '你不应该来的，林雨。' Two voices; one man.
outline.notes: The two voices merge here — the ambiguity tightens instead of resolving.
outline.recap: Near midnight old Zhou stops where the water grows shallow; the sea draws back, slowly then fast, and a path of stones rises from the black water all the way to the two rocks, and even Zhou's hands tremble as he reminds her: one hour; Lin Yu walks the wet, slippery path alone, bell in hand and phone off, remembering every A Ye — "go back", the question about rain, his first "thank you", the threat in the water, the bloody knife, the cold hands on her throat, the low voice; she reaches the rocks, touches the real gate for the first time, the bell rings, and she steps through — not into the grey sea but into a cave of total darkness, where chains drag closer and a voice says "you came" in the low voice and then "you shouldn't have come, Lin Yu" in A Ye's words: the two voices belong to one man.

outline.title: 黑暗里
outline.summary: In total darkness, their first real meeting. He is angry, then admits the low voice was also him: after 300 years, half of him wants out at any cost, half only wants her to live, and he doesn't know which is him. She finds him by the sound of the chains and touches his face; he finds the red line on her wrist and lays it on the identical one under his chain.
scenes: '阿夜？' No answer; only chains moving left and right in the dark like someone pacing. Then his voice, suddenly close, fast, angry: '我说了多少次？别来，别来，别来！你为什么从来不听？'

She isn't angry: in ten years she has never been this close — close enough to hear him breathe. 'Because you also told me to come. The voice behind the gate. That was you too, wasn't it?' Long silence. '对。那也是我。'

Why? 'Three hundred years alone in a place this dark. Half of me wants out every day — any way, no matter what happens to you. The other half listened to you every night — rain, noodles, your 奶奶 — and only wants you to live.' 'Which half is you?' '我不知道。三百年了，我也不知道。'
She can't see, but she doesn't stop: one step, another, hands out in front. The chains come closer. Her hand touches something: a hand, cold and large, with a chain on it. They both freeze.
Slowly she moves her hand up: his shoulder, then his face — thin, long hair, wet. Sea water, or something else. '阿夜，是你。' '是我。'

He takes her left hand and lays a finger on the red line; then puts her hand on his own left wrist: under the chain, the same line in the same place, like two people wearing the same watch. For ten years there was water between them; now there is not even that. Outside, faintly, the sea.
outline.notes: Both halves confessed by him — the reader still can't tell which will win.
outline.recap: In the pitch-dark cave A Ye is close and furious — "how many times did I say don't come?" — but admits the low voice that called her was also him: after 300 years alone in the dark, having forgotten every face in Haicheng and his own name, half of him wants out at any cost and called to her, knowing all he knew; the other half listened to her talk of rain and noodles and only wants her to live to be very old; he doesn't know which half is him; she keeps walking toward the sound of the chains, finds his cold hand, his shoulder, his thin wet face — "it's you" — and he lays her wrist's red line against the identical one under his chain: "for ten years, when you hurt, I hurt"; for the first time there is not even water between them, and outside the sea sounds a little closer.

outline.title: 火是我的
outline.summary: She asks: did you burn 海城? He says yes — what they say is true, the fire was his; the man he was then loved no one. But ten years of a girl describing rain made him someone who would rather stay chained another 300 years than kill her. He tells her to leave while he is still this self. She stays. Then he asks to see her, once. Her hand finds the phone.
scenes: '三百年前，海城的火……是你放的吗？' He doesn't answer at once. The cave is so quiet she can hear the sea outside — a little closer than before.
'是。他们说的都是真的。火是我的。' Her hand stays on his face. 'I won't tell you I'm a good man, because I'm not, so I can't say it.'
The man of 300 years ago: he remembers him — cold, angry, loved no one, thought nothing in the world mattered more than himself. 'And now?' 'Now I don't know who I am.'

'Ten years ago a girl sat on the other side of the water and told me what rain was like. Since then I've waited every day for night. I didn't know a person could wait for another person like that.' Her tears fall. 'I'd rather stay here another three hundred years than have you die by my hands.' 'But you called me.' 'Yes. So go now. I don't know how much longer this me will last.'

She doesn't go. They stand without speaking; the sea a little closer again. Then, very quietly: '林雨。' '我在。' '让我看你一次。只看一次。I don't want 水里的你 — I want you. Three hundred years I haven't seen anyone's face. Once.'

Her heart stops. Her hand goes slowly into her pocket and closes on the phone. In the dark she doesn't know which of him is asking: the one who listened to her talk about rain and wants to see her face before he dies — or the one who set the fire and has waited three hundred years for exactly this.
outline.notes: The dark reading is confirmed about the past; the present stays open until the next chapter.
outline.recap: Lin Yu asks if he set the fire 300 years ago, and A Ye says yes — it was his: he came out of the sea knowing nothing, the town shunned him and children threw stones, only the girl fed him and taught him to speak and laugh; when the town locked her up for talking to him, he was so angry he let the fire out — but it grew beyond him, and he spent all his strength pulling half of it back while the other half burned all night (so the fire was both leaving and returning to his hands); fearing his own fire, he asked her to lock him, and she spoke the curse for the town's sake — "she gave it to me, and I wanted it"; the man he was then loved no one, but ten years of her stories taught him to wait for someone and not want to leave for her sake, so he'd rather stay 300 more years than kill her; he tells her to go while "this me" lasts; she stays; and then, very quietly, he asks to see her — just once — and her hand closes on the phone, not knowing which of him is asking.

outline.title: 灯
outline.summary: She sees the loophole would only make her the one hiding, and refuses it: she turns on the light. He sees her; the lock breaks; the chains fall. His right hand, against his will, takes up the ancient knife she once used to cut her palm. She does not run; she holds his knife hand and tells him neither of them is who they were 300 years ago. A drop of her blood falls — and he throws the knife into the sea. His fire goes out for good. The tide returns; they run along the drowning path toward 小美's lamp; behind them the gate is gone.
scenes: Her reasoning, short: she found the little door — no light, no seeing, no lock, no knife; she could hold his hand in the dark till the tide and come back next year. But for ten years he hid from her; now she would be hiding from him. 'If the one I love is someone I don't dare look at, who is it I love?'

'阿夜，你也看看我吧。' She turns on the phone light. The whole cave fills with light. He is thinner and more tired than she imagined, pale as if he hasn't seen the sun in a long time — and the face she drew a hundred times. His eyes look straight at her. '林雨……你比水里的你好看。'

A sound like thunder: the lock. The chains break one by one and fall — hands, feet. He looks at his empty hands. Then his face changes: his right hand moves by itself, reaching to the stone floor where an old, old knife lies — the knife she used 300 years ago. It lifts.

'跑！林雨，快跑！' His left hand drags at his right and can't hold it. She doesn't run. She takes his knife hand in both of hers. The blade comes to her throat; she feels its cold. 'You are not the man of 300 years ago. I'm not that girl. She said the curse, not me.' 'I can't stop —' 'You can. I'm not afraid of you. I believe you.'

The blade touches her neck; one drop of blood runs down — like the blood on the lock 300 years ago. He cries out, a sound like two men at once, and with all his strength pulls the knife away, turns, and throws it out of the cave into the sea. A little fire flares in both his hands, small and red, bright one last time — and goes out. His hands shake, and the shaking is his own. '他走了。三百年前的那个人……走了。'

Water sound: the tide is back. They run: through the gate, onto the path, sea at their feet, their knees, cold as winter ice. She can't see the path but sees a light far away — 小美, still there. They run toward it. She looks back once: the two black rocks are still there; the gate between them is gone.
outline.notes: Resolution per notes.ending. Invert his refrain: at the end of the run he says '你过来' or takes her hand — he now goes toward her.
outline.recap: Lin Yu realises the darkness loophole would only make her the one hiding — "if the one I love is someone I don't dare look at, who is it I love?" — and turns on her phone light; she sees A Ye, thinner and paler than she imagined, in 300-year-old clothes, the face she drew hundreds of times, and he looks straight at her: "you're lovelier than the you in the water"; the lock breaks with a sound like thunder and every chain falls; then his right hand, against his will, takes up the ancient knife she once cut her palm with and lifts it while he drags at it with his left and begs her to run; she doesn't, holds his knife hand with both of hers and tells him neither of them is who they were 300 years ago; the blade touches her neck and a drop of blood falls — he cries out like two men at once, tears the knife away and hurls it through the gate into the sea; a last flicker of fire leaves his hands for good — "he's gone, the man from 300 years ago"; the tide returns, and for the first time in ten years he holds out his hand and says "come here"; they run the drowning path toward Xiaomei's lamp, and behind them the gate between the rocks is gone.

outline.title: 门这边
outline.summary: Dawn: 小美 and 老周 see two people come out of the sea; 小美 touches his arm to be sure he is real; 阿夜 weeps at his first sunrise in 300 years. Half a year later he lives with 林雨 in 奶奶's house, mending nets with 老周, laughing, his hands without fire; in his first rain he finds it soft, as she said. He no longer dreams; she sometimes still dreams of the empty chains. Who he was she knows; who he is, he chooses every day. She writes one last post.
scenes: Waist-deep water, legs numb; she never lets go of his hand. 小美 runs into the sea crying her name; 老周's boat close by. 小美 hugs her — then sees the man beside her, reaches out and touches his arm: '是真的。他是真的。'

Sunrise: first a red line on the sea, then bigger, brighter — red, yellow, gold. 阿夜 doesn't move; tears run down. '三百年，我忘了，太阳是这样的。' 老周 puts his coat over him, looks at him like an old story, asks nothing: '先回家吧。吃点儿东西。'
Half a year later: 阿夜 lives in 奶奶's old house, and so does 我; she quit the city and teaches drawing at the 海城 primary school. 小美 visits every holiday and still calls him '梦里的那个人'.

阿夜 goes out with 老周 every day, mending nets and boats; at first he gets everything in a mess, 老周 scolds, he laughs — he laughs every day now. No more fire in his hands: in winter he holds them to the stove and waits for them to warm, like anyone.

April, their first rain: he runs outside, face up, standing in it a long time. Back in, hair wet: '跟你说的一样。很软。像有人在你的脸上轻轻地说话。' She makes hot noodles; they eat and listen to the rain. He says he doesn't dream anymore. She still does, sometimes: the grey sea, the gate, the chains lying empty, nobody there. Maybe the place the old him left behind.

Is he a good man? The fire was his; he never denied it. But ten years ago someone sat beyond the water asking what rain was like. Who he was, she knows; who he is, he chooses every day — and so does she: the girl of 300 years ago spoke the curse; she chose the light. Last night she opened the website and wrote《我找到他了》: '…我找到他了。他没有杀我。现在他就坐在我的旁边，在学用筷子吃面条儿……另：我可以告诉你们更多的细节。' She pressed send. Outside, it was raining again.
outline.notes: Echo ch1 (the post, pressing send), ch4 (rain is soft like someone speaking softly to your face), ch3 (the sun he never had).
outline.recap: At dawn they wade ashore; Xiaomei touches A Ye's arm to be sure he is real, and he weeps at his first sunrise in 300 years; half a year later he lives with Lin Yu in Grandma's old house — she has left the city to teach drawing at the Haicheng primary school, Xiaomei visits every holiday and still calls him "the man from the dream"; at first he can't use chopsticks or cross a road, stares at his face in a mirror, and finds his first noodles "just as you said"; he mends nets with old Zhou, laughing every day, his hands without fire; at Grandma's grave he thanks her for keeping the bell — and for keeping Lin Yu; in their first April rain he stands outside until soaked and finds it soft "like someone speaking softly to your face"; he no longer dreams, while she sometimes dreams of empty chains behind the gate; who he was she knows — who he is, he chooses every day, as she chose the light; she writes a new post, "I found him. He did not kill me… P.S. I can tell you more details," and outside it is raining again.
